title: Toronto Police Issue Warrant for Indian Man Who Posed as Psychic in Fraud Scheme
excerpt: A man from India allegedly conned a Toronto victim out of money by offering fake spiritual protection, prompting police to issue an arrest warrant.
body:
• Toronto Police have issued an arrest warrant for an Indian man accused of posing as a psychic and defrauding a victim.
  • The suspect allegedly offered the victim "spiritual protection" to gain trust before extracting money.
  • The case fits a pattern of psychic and spiritual fraud that Toronto Police have flagged as a growing concern.
  • Police are urging anyone with information to come forward as the suspect remains at large.

Toronto Police have issued an arrest warrant for an Indian man accused of posing as a psychic and defrauding a victim by offering fake spiritual protection, authorities announced this week.

The Alleged Scheme

According to Toronto Police, the suspect approached the victim and presented himself as a spiritual healer with supernatural abilities. He allegedly told the victim they were in danger and offered "spiritual protection" — a ruse designed to build trust and dependency before extracting money.

"He allegedly told the victim they were in danger and offered "spiritual protection" — a ruse designed to build trust and dependency before extracting money."

The investigation revealed a calculated pattern: the suspect used cultural familiarity and spiritual language to establish credibility, then escalated demands for payment under the guise of rituals and protective services. Police did not disclose the exact amount defrauded but described the scheme as a significant financial fraud.

A Growing Pattern

Toronto Police have flagged psychic and spiritual fraud as a growing concern in the Greater Toronto Area, where a large South Asian diaspora can sometimes be targeted through culturally specific scams. Similar cases have been reported in other major North American cities with significant Indian populations.

Law enforcement agencies in Canada have noted an increase in fraud schemes that exploit cultural trust — including fake pandit or astrologer scams, marriage fraud, and immigration-related cons targeting South Asian communities.

What the Diaspora Should Know

Community leaders in the GTA have urged members of the Indian diaspora to exercise caution when approached by unknown individuals claiming spiritual abilities. Legitimate spiritual practitioners, they note, do not typically approach strangers with unsolicited warnings of danger.

Toronto Police are asking anyone with information about the suspect to contact their local division or Crime Stoppers at 416-222-TIPS (8477). The investigation remains active.
